ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In Figure B, the horizontal axis is the distance from the city center, and the vertical axis is the R value; the R value curves for 1996 and 2001 both show that as the distance from the city center increases, they first rise, reach a peak, and then decline. Then reason: The R value represents the ratio of manufacturing population density to service-industry employment population density. The position of the maximum R value can be understood as the urban edge or urban-rural transition zone where manufacturing is most prominent relative to services. This peak value moving away from the city center shows that the urban edge belt moved outward, reflecting that the central urban area of Beijing expanded and, at the same time, the urbanization level of the suburbs increased.
